title: प्रधानमन्त्री रोजगार कार्यक्रमको विश्लेषण: Analysis of Prime Minister Employment Programme
nepali: मुलुकमा व्याप्त निरपेक्ष गरिबी घटाउने, बेरोजगारी कम गर्ने, वित्तीय दिगोपन कायम हुने गरी सामाजिक संरक्षणको दायरा विस्तार गर्ने र स्थानीयस्तरमा ससाना सार्वजनिक भौतिक पूर्वाधारलाई स्थानीय जनताकै सहभागितामा व्यवस्थित गर्ने उद्देश्यले सङ्‍घीय सरकारको कार्यक्रमको रूपमा एकै पटक ७५३ ओटै स्थानीय तहमा लागु गर्ने गरी प्रधानमन्त्री रोजागार कार्यक्रमको सुरुवात आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ मा गरिएको थियो। नेपालको संविधानको धारा ३३ मा उल्लिखित रोजगारीको हकको कार्यान्वयनको लागि समेत यसको कार्यान्वयन गर्नुपरेको हो। यस लेखमा यस कार्यक्रमका सबल र दुर्बल पक्षहरूका साथै अवसर र चुनौतीहरूको विश्लेषण गरिएको छ।विगत चार वर्षमा यस कार्यक्रमले हासिल गरेका उपलब्धि सन्तोषजनक भएतापनि यसका दुर्बल पक्षलाई सबल पक्षमा र चुनौतीलाई अवसरमा रूपान्तरण गर्ने गरी कार्यक्रमका विविध पक्षमा निरन्तर सुधार गरी यसलाई थप प्रभावकारी बनाउनु जरूरी देखिन्छ।
american_english: The Prime Minister Employment Programme was launched in fiscal year 2075/76 BS as a federal government program aimed at reducing widespread absolute poverty in the country, reducing unemployment, ensuring financial sustainability while expanding social protection coverage, and organizing small public physical infrastructure at the local level with local people's participation. It was implemented at once in all 753 local levels as a federal government program, and this is also necessary for the implementation of the right to employment stipulated in Article 33 of the Constitution of Nepal. This article analyzes the strengths and weaknesses as well as the opportunities and challenges of this program. In the past four years, although the achievements of this program have been satisfactory, there is a need to continuously improve various aspects of the program to make its weaknesses stronger and turn challenges into opportunities to make it more effective.
british_english: The Prime Minister's Employment Programme commenced operations in the fiscal year 2075/76 BS as a federal initiative targeting the reduction of pervasive poverty, curbing unemployment levels, ensuring fiscal viability alongside expanding social protection mechanisms, and organising minor public infrastructure projects at local administrative tiers involving community participation. This comprehensive programme was simultaneously rolled out across all 753 local governance units, aligning with constitutional imperatives outlined in Article 33 concerning employment rights. The analysis herein examines programmatic strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and challenges. Despite commendable achievements over the past four years, continuous improvement across multiple programme dimensions remains essential to transform vulnerabilities into strengths and convert obstacles into opportunities.

informal_english: The Prime Minister Employment Programme was kicked off in the fiscal year 2075/76 BS as a federal government initiative aimed at tackling widespread poverty, cutting down unemployment, making sure we can keep finances stable while expanding social safety nets, and organizing small public infrastructure projects at the local level with help from local people. This program was rolled out all at once across every one of the 753 local levels as part of the federal government's efforts, and it's also crucial for making good on the employment rights promised in Article 33 of Nepal's Constitution. In this article, I break down the program's strengths and weaknesses, along with the opportunities and challenges it faces. Even though the program has achieved some good results over the past four years, there's still a need to keep working on improving different parts of it to turn its weaknesses into strengths and challenges into chances to make it work even better.
